/-!
# Conjecture 6.5

by R. Bieri

Is it the case that every soluble group $G$ of type $(FP)_{\infty}$ is *constructible* in the
sense of G. Baumslag, R. Bieri, *Math. Z.* **151**, no. 3 (1976), 249–257? In other words, can
$G$ be built up from the trivial group in terms of finite extensions and $HNN$-extensions?

A group $G$ is of type $(FP)_{\infty}$ if the trivial $\mathbb{Z}G$-module $\mathbb{Z}$ admits a
projective resolution
$$\cdots \to P_n \to \cdots \to P_1 \to P_0 \to \mathbb{Z} \to 0$$
in which every $P_n$ is a finitely generated projective $\mathbb{Z}G$-module.

Following Baumslag and Bieri, the class of constructible groups is the smallest class of groups
that contains the trivial group and is closed under finite extensions and under forming
$HNN$-extensions whose base group and associated subgroups belong to the class. Baumslag and
Bieri proved that constructible soluble groups are of type $(FP)_{\infty}$; the problem asks for
the converse.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 6.5
- G. Baumslag, R. Bieri, *Constructable solvable groups*, Math. Z. **151** (1976), no. 3, 249–257
-/

def IsFPInfinity (G : Type) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ P : ProjectiveResolution
      (ModuleCat.of (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) (Representation.trivial ℤ G ℤ).asModule),
    ∀ n : ℕ, Module.Finite (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) (P.complex.X n)
blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is of type $(FP)_{\infty}$ if the trivial $\mathbb{Z}G$-module $\mathbb{Z}$ has a
projective resolution by finitely generated projective $\mathbb{Z}G$-modules, i.e. there is an
exact sequence $\cdots \to P_1 \to P_0 \to \mathbb{Z} \to 0$ of $\mathbb{Z}G$-modules with every

Here the group ring $\mathbb{Z}G$ is `MonoidAlgebra ℤ G` and the trivial module $\mathbb{Z}$ is

justification.closest_existing_considered: `CategoryTheory.ProjectiveResolution` / `HasProjectiveResolution` (no finiteness condition), `Rep.trivial` with `Rep ℤ G` (finite generation over ℤG awkward to express there), `groupCohomology` machinery (does not encode FP_n). Built on `ProjectiveResolution` in `ModuleCat (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G)` plus `Module.Finite`.

justification.why_needed: Homological finiteness type FP_∞ of a group (trivial ℤG-module ℤ has a projective resolution by finitely generated projective ℤG-modules) is not in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib.

inductive IsConstructible : (G : Type u) → [Group G] → Prop
  /-- The trivial group is constructible. -/
  | trivial (G : Type u) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] : IsConstructible G
  /-- Constructibility is invariant under isomorphism. -/
  | of_mulEquiv {G H : Type u} [Group G] [Group H] (e : G ≃* H) :
      IsConstructible G → IsConstructible H
  /-- A finite extension of a constructible group is constructible. -/
  | finiteExtension {G : Type u} [Group G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] [N.FiniteIndex] :
      IsConstructible N → IsConstructible G
  /-- An $HNN$-extension with constructible base group and constructible associated subgroups
  is constructible. -/
  | hnn {B : Type u} [Group B] (A A' : Subgroup B) (φ : A ≃* A') :
      IsConstructible B → IsConstructible A → IsConstructible A' →
      IsConstructible (HNNExtension B A A' φ)
blocks.docstring:
The constructible groups of Baumslag and Bieri: the smallest class of groups which contains the
trivial group and is closed under

* finite extensions: if $N \trianglelefteq G$ has finite index and $N$ is constructible, then so
  is $G$;
* $HNN$-extensions: if $B$ is constructible and $\varphi \colon A \to A'$ is an isomorphism between
  constructible subgroups $A, A' \le B$, then the $HNN$-extension
  $\langle B, t \mid t a t^{-1} = \varphi(a),\ a \in A \rangle$ is constructible.

The class is also closed under isomorphism, so that constructibility does not depend on the
particular model of a group.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `HNNExtension` (the construction, but no class closure), `Subgroup.FiniteIndex`/`Subgroup.Normal` (finite extensions), `IsSolvable`, `Group.FG`; no existing predicate captures the inductive closure, so an inductive Prop was defined using these.
justification.name: Kourovka.«6.5».IsConstructible
justification.why_needed: The Baumslag–Bieri class of constructible groups (smallest class containing the trivial group, closed under finite extensions and HNN-extensions with base and associated subgroups in the class) is not in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib.

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsConstructible.multiplicative_int : IsConstructible (Multiplicative ℤ) :=
  let e : HNNExtension PUnit (⊥ : Subgroup PUnit) ⊥ (MulEquiv.refl _) ≃* Multiplicative ℤ :=
    MonoidHom.toMulEquiv (HNNExtension.lift 1 (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1) (fun _ => by simp))
      (zpowersHom _ HNNExtension.t)
      (HNNExtension.hom_ext
        (by ext g; simp [Subsingleton.elim g 1, ← MonoidHom.map_one HNNExtension.of]) (by simp))
      (by ext; simp)
  .of_mulEquiv e (.hnn _ _ _ (.trivial _) (.trivial _) (.trivial _))

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFPInfinity_of_subsingleton (G : Type) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] :
    IsFPInfinity G := by
  haveI : Unique G := ⟨⟨1⟩, fun _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩
  set ρ := Representation.trivial ℤ G ℤ
  have key (r : MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) (x : ρ.asModule) :
      r • x = ρ.asModuleEquiv.symm (r default * ρ.asModuleEquiv x) := by
    conv_lhs => rw [Finsupp.unique_single r]
    rw [Representation.single_smul]
    rfl
  let e : MonoidAlgebra ℤ G ≃ₗ[MonoidAlgebra ℤ G] ρ.asModule :=
    LinearEquiv.ofBijective (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton _ _ (ρ.asModuleEquiv.symm 1))
      ⟨fun r s h => ?_, fun x => ⟨MonoidAlgebra.single default (ρ.asModuleEquiv x), ?_⟩⟩
  · haveI : Module.Projective (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) ρ.asModule := Module.Projective.of_equiv e
    haveI : Module.Finite (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) ρ.asModule := Module.Finite.equiv e
    set Z := ModuleCat.of (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) ρ.asModule
    refine ⟨ProjectiveResolution.self Z, fun n => ?_⟩
    cases n with
    | zero =>
      exact Module.Finite.equiv
        (HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (ComplexShape.down ℕ) 0 Z).toLinearEquiv.symm
    | succ n =>
      haveI : Subsingleton ((ProjectiveResolution.self Z).complex.X (n + 1)) :=
        ModuleCat.subsingleton_of_isZero
          (HomologicalComplex.isZero_single_obj_X (ComplexShape.down ℕ) 0 Z (n + 1) (by simp))
      exact Module.Finite.of_finite
  · simp only [LinearMap.toSpanSingleton_apply, key, LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, mul_one,
      EmbeddingLike.apply_eq_iff_eq] at h
    rw [Finsupp.unique_single r, Finsupp.unique_single s, h]
  · simp only [LinearMap.toSpanSingleton_apply, key, LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, mul_one,
      Finsupp.single_eq_same]
    exact ρ.asModuleEquiv.symm_apply_apply x

claims.decomposer_note: Single unlettered yes/no question (Bieri's conjecture), Prop: ∀ G, IsSolvable G → G of type FP_∞ (trivial ZG-module Z has a resolution by finitely generated projective ZG-modules in every degree) → G constructible; the 'In other words' sentence is not a separate question but the Baumslag–Bieri definition of constructible (smallest class of groups containing the trivial group, closed under finite extensions and under HNN-extensions with base and associated subgroups in the class), which is not in Mathlib and must be defined (Mathlib has HNNExtension and IsSolvable but neither FP_∞ nor constructibility); note the converse (constructible soluble ⇒ FP_∞) is a Baumslag–Bieri theorem and not part of the question.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful shape `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsSolvable G → FP_∞ G → Constructible G` (only the asked direction; converse excluded). c08's file was used as the base: FP_∞ as a Mathlib `ProjectiveResolution` of `ModuleCat.of (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) (Representation.trivial ℤ G ℤ).asModule` with `Module.Finite` in every degree (Bieri's definition; categorical Projective = Module.Projective in ModuleCat), and an isomorphism-closed inductive `IsConstructible` with trivial group, finite extensions (normal finite-index subgroup in the class) and Mathlib `HNNExtension` with base and associated subgroups in the class. Edits: the `hnn` constructor requires both associated subgroups A and A' to be constructible (taken from c02/c05/c07, mirroring the Baumslag–Bieri wording; equivalent to c08's version via iso-closure), and c07's proof that the trivial group is FP_∞ was adapted (ULift removed) as a test. Kept c08's/c02's API tests (finite groups and ℤ are constructible). Compiles with `lake --wfail build` and only the expected sorry warning.

/-!
# Conjecture 6.5

by R. Bieri

Is it the case that every soluble group $G$ of type $(FP)_{\infty}$ is *constructible* in the
sense of G. Baumslag, R. Bieri, *Math. Z.* **151**, no. 3 (1976), 249–257? In other words, can
$G$ be built up from the trivial group in terms of finite extensions and $HNN$-extensions?

A group $G$ is of type $(FP)_{\infty}$ if the trivial $\mathbb{Z}G$-module $\mathbb{Z}$ admits a
projective resolution
$$\cdots \to P_n \to \cdots \to P_1 \to P_0 \to \mathbb{Z} \to 0$$
in which every $P_n$ is a finitely generated projective $\mathbb{Z}G$-module.

Following Baumslag and Bieri, the class of constructible groups is the smallest class of groups
that contains the trivial group and is closed under finite extensions and under forming
$HNN$-extensions whose base group and associated subgroups belong to the class. Baumslag and

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 6.5
- G. Baumslag, R. Bieri, *Constructable solvable groups*, Math. Z. **151** (1976), no. 3, 249–257
-/

namespace Kourovka.«6.5»

open CategoryTheory

universe u

/--
A group $G$ is of type $(FP)_{\infty}$ if the trivial $\mathbb{Z}G$-module $\mathbb{Z}$ has a
projective resolution by finitely generated projective $\mathbb{Z}G$-modules, i.e. there is an
exact sequence $\cdots \to P_1 \to P_0 \to \mathbb{Z} \to 0$ of $\mathbb{Z}G$-modules with every
$P_n$ finitely generated and projective.

Here the group ring $\mathbb{Z}G$ is `MonoidAlgebra ℤ G` and the trivial module $\mathbb{Z}$ is
`(Representation.trivial ℤ G ℤ).asModule`.
-/
def IsFPInfinity (G : Type) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ P : ProjectiveResolution
      (ModuleCat.of (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) (Representation.trivial ℤ G ℤ).asModule),
    ∀ n : ℕ, Module.Finite (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) (P.complex.X n)

/--
The constructible groups of Baumslag and Bieri: the smallest class of groups which contains the
trivial group and is closed under

* finite extensions: if $N \trianglelefteq G$ has finite index and $N$ is constructible, then so
  is $G$;
* $HNN$-extensions: if $B$ is constructible and $\varphi \colon A \to A'$ is an isomorphism between
  constructible subgroups $A, A' \le B$, then the $HNN$-extension
  $\langle B, t \mid t a t^{-1} = \varphi(a),\ a \in A \rangle$ is constructible.

The class is also closed under isomorphism, so that constructibility does not depend on the
particular model of a group.
-/
inductive IsConstructible : (G : Type u) → [Group G] → Prop
  /-- The trivial group is constructible. -/
  | trivial (G : Type u) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] : IsConstructible G
  /-- Constructibility is invariant under isomorphism. -/
  | of_mulEquiv {G H : Type u} [Group G] [Group H] (e : G ≃* H) :
      IsConstructible G → IsConstructible H
  /-- A finite extension of a constructible group is constructible. -/
  | finiteExtension {G : Type u} [Group G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] [N.FiniteIndex] :
      IsConstructible N → IsConstructible G
  /-- An $HNN$-extension with constructible base group and constructible associated subgroups
  is constructible. -/
  | hnn {B : Type u} [Group B] (A A' : Subgroup B) (φ : A ≃* A') :
      IsConstructible B → IsConstructible A → IsConstructible A' →
      IsConstructible (HNNExtension B A A' φ)

/-- Every finite group is constructible, being a finite extension of the trivial group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsConstructible.of_finite (G : Type u) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsConstructible G :=
  .finiteExtension (⊥ : Subgroup G) (.trivial _)

/-- The infinite cyclic group is constructible, being an $HNN$-extension of the trivial group. -/

    MonoidHom.toMulEquiv (HNNExtension.lift 1 (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1) (fun _ => by simp))

      (HNNExtension.hom_ext

      (by ext; simp)
  .of_mulEquiv e (.hnn _ _ _ (.trivial _) (.trivial _) (.trivial _))

/-- The trivial group is of type $(FP)_\infty$: $\mathbb{Z}$ is a free module of rank one over
$\mathbb{Z}[1] \cong \mathbb{Z}$, so it is its own resolution. -/

theorem isFPInfinity_of_subsingleton (G : Type) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] :

    set Z := ModuleCat.of (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) ρ.asModule
    refine ⟨ProjectiveResolution.self Z, fun n => ?_⟩
    cases n with
    | zero =>
      exact Module.Finite.equiv
        (HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (ComplexShape.down ℕ) 0 Z).toLinearEquiv.symm
    | succ n =>
      haveI : Subsingleton ((ProjectiveResolution.self Z).complex.X (n + 1)) :=
        ModuleCat.subsingleton_of_isZero
          (HomologicalComplex.isZero_single_obj_X (ComplexShape.down ℕ) 0 Z (n + 1) (by simp))
      exact Module.Finite.of_finite
  · simp only [LinearMap.toSpanSingleton_apply, key, LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, mul_one,
      EmbeddingLike.apply_eq_iff_eq] at h

  · simp only [LinearMap.toSpanSingleton_apply, key, LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, mul_one,
      Finsupp.single_eq_same]
    exact ρ.asModuleEquiv.symm_apply_apply x

/--
Is it the case that every soluble group $G$ of type $(FP)_{\infty}$ is constructible in the sense
of Baumslag and Bieri? In other words, can $G$ be built up from the trivial group in terms of
finite extensions and $HNN$-extensions?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.5» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsSolvable G → IsFPInfinity G → IsConstructible G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.5»

items: "Finite extension" is read in the class-of-groups sense: G is a finite extension of N when N ⊴ G is a normal subgroup of finite index (`[N.Normal] [N.FiniteIndex]`). If Baumslag–Bieri intended an arbitrary (not necessarily normal) finite-index subgroup, the class could a priori be larger; a reviewer with access to Math. Z. 151 (1976) should check the exact wording.

HNN closure uses Mathlib's `HNNExtension B A A' φ` (one stable letter, `φ : A ≃* A'`) and requires the base `B` and the associated subgroup `A` to be constructible; `A'` is isomorphic to `A` via `φ` and is constructible by the isomorphism-closure constructor, so it is not listed as a separate hypothesis. Following the decomposition table, associated subgroups are required to lie in the class (not merely to be finitely generated).

An explicit isomorphism-closure constructor `of_mulEquiv` is included so that `IsConstructible` is a property of abstract groups (otherwise e.g. `Multiplicative ℤ` would not be constructible, only the literal `HNNExtension PUnit ⊥ ⊥ _`). Being an inductive Prop, `IsConstructible` is the smallest such class.
The trivial group is encoded as `[Subsingleton G]` in the `trivial` constructor.

Type (FP)_∞ is defined directly as: there exists a projective resolution of the trivial ℤG-module ℤ (Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.ProjectiveResolution` in `ModuleCat (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G)`, i.e. a chain complex of projectives quasi-isomorphic to ℤ in degree 0) all of whose terms are finitely generated (`Module.Finite`). This is Baumslag–Bieri's phrasing ('finitely generated in every dimension') and is equivalent to 'FP_n for all n'.
The trivial module is `(Representation.trivial ℤ G ℤ).asModule` (checked: `MonoidAlgebra.of ℤ G g • v = v`). The group ring ℤG is `MonoidAlgebra ℤ G`.

Groups are quantified over `Type` (universe 0), consistent with the other Kourovka files; `IsFPInfinity` is stated for `G : Type` because ℤ lives in `Type 0` and `ModuleCat.of` needs the module in the same universe as the ring. `IsConstructible` is universe polymorphic.

Added a proven API lemma (`IsConstructible.of_finite`: finite groups are constructible) and a proven test (`IsConstructible.multiplicative_int`: the infinite cyclic group is constructible as an HNN-extension of the trivial group) to exercise the new definition.

reviewer_notes: 1) Status: the task and the Kourovka Notebook v46 record 6.5 as open, so the file uses `research open` and `answer(sorry)`. However, c07 correctly flags that the literature appears to have settled this affirmatively: Kropholler (JPAA 1986, for finite torsion-free rank) together with Kropholler (Bull. LMS 25, 1993, 'Soluble groups of type (FP)_∞ have finite torsion-free rank') gives that every soluble group of type FP_∞ is constructible. Maintainers may wish to retag as `research solved` with `answer(True)`; I followed the source's recorded status. 2) 'Finite extension' is read as: N normal of finite index in G with N constructible. The alternative reading (any finite-index subgroup in the class) generates the same class of soluble groups (c05's argument checks out: every HNN step in a soluble construction is ascending, and the normal-reading class of soluble groups is closed under finite-index subgroups by induction; then use the normal core), so the conjecture's meaning is unaffected. 3) Quantification over `G : Type` follows the other Kourovka files; no generality is lost since soluble FP_∞ groups are countable and both predicates are isomorphism-invariant. 4) `IsConstructible` is universe-polymorphic but used at universe 0; the trivial group is encoded as any `Subsingleton` group. 5) c01's impredicative encoding and c03/c04/c06's `Rep ℤ G` encoding of FP_∞ are also faithful; c05's hand-rolled exact sequence is faithful but more verbose. No candidate was judged unfaithful.
